svg.title: BLUELINE — the live clock loop
svg.desc: How the animatic plays the rendered boards in time with Ableton: the Ableton Set's Transport (MASTER) and ClipScan (SCANNER, on the Boards track) devices emit OSC over UDP port 9001 to the relay osc_ws_relay.py, which rebroadcasts every message as JSON over WebSocket port 8770 to the animatic.html browser player, which builds its storyboard from the Boards scan and shows each board in time. The locked clock: frames per beat = (fps x 60) / tempo = 12, whole, so every clip lands on an exact frame.
svg.text: BLUELINE · THE LIVE CLOCK LOOP
how the animatic plays the rendered boards in time with Ableton — the music leads, the boards follow
ABLETON LIVE — YOUR SET · THE SOURCE OF TRUTH THAT IS NOT THE PIXELS
Blueline Transport [MASTER] · on a clock track · one per Set
reads the tempo + the arrangement Locators (the sections)
Blueline ClipScan [SCANNER] · on the Boards track · one per content track
reads its own 6 MIDI clips — name = the prompt, position+length = the timing
OSC / UDP · 127.0.0.1:9001 — one small local hop
/transport/bible tempo · fps · sig on load / tempo change
/transport/beat bar · beat · playing ~20 Hz while running
/transport/section name · start · length on entering a Locator
/Boards/scan · clip×6 · scan_end one-shot, on Stop / SCAN
the scan is namespaced by the track name → a track called “Boards” emits /Boards/* (placement is the config)
RELAY · osc_ws_relay.py (Shop machinery, no GPU)
rebroadcasts every OSC message as JSON to all browsers · also serves /animatic and /boards
git is ground truth; the wire is just status — message jitter never reaches the deterministic render
WebSocket / JSON · 127.0.0.1:8770/ws
the same messages, fanned out to every connected browser (clock client · previz · animatic · the render runner)
ANIMATIC · animatic.html (the browser player)
▸ builds its storyboard from the Boards scan — 6 Live clips → the 6 rendered boards
▸ the playhead (/transport/beat) chooses which board is on screen, right now
▸ renders the real board PNG in time, beat-locked — an instrument, not a video
filmstrip of all 6 · determinism HUD · section read-out · every scanner track as a lane
THE LOCKED CLOCK — what makes it an instrument
frames_per_beat = (fps × 60) ÷ tempo = (24 × 60) ÷ 120 = 12 · whole ✓ (frames/sec × sec/min ÷ beats/min)
frame = clip_start_beats × frames_per_beat → a clip at bar 5 = 16 beats → frame 192
the clip's position + length is the EDIT · the clip's name is the CONTENT — two independent layers
Loudon Live · Autodidact Polymaths
BLUELINE · animatic · Track III clock
